diagnostic.root_cause: FOV relaxation was doing double duty: (1) FOV awareness and (2) beneficial helix turn inflation. Removing it exposed helix to TOPP over-compression. max_compression 0.65→0.68 partially compensated but helix gates 7-12 still regressed 0.025-0.052m each.
architectural_issues: Helix needs dedicated turn inflation — currently only gets generic treatment via curvature-based TOPP speed limits
max_compression in TOPP is the binding constraint on helix speed, not curvature-based limits
Gate-4 still worst at 0.413m — S-turn geometry inherently challenging
Avg error 0.248m is barely below 0.25m aspirational — next iteration should recover accuracy
critic_findings: FOV relaxation removal successfully simplified pipeline from 4→3 stages
Trajectory generation 27% faster (47ms vs 64ms) due to removed intermediate generation
a_centripetal parameter has no effect when max_compression is binding — indicates TOPP floor is too dominant

improvements_backlog.description: Helix accuracy recovery — gates 7-12 regressed 0.025-0.052m each from FOV relaxation removal
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Add helix-specific inflation in _inflate_sharp_turns for moderate-angle turns (20-40°). Currently only >60° turns get angle-based inflation.
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Helix gates recover to iter 16 levels, avg error 0.248→0.235m

improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Increase gate-4 specific inflation or adjust racing line lateral offset

improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Better FOV awareness with zero time cost

improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Run L-BFGS from 5-10 random initializations, score by TOPP-computed race time
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Find better racing line basins, potential 0.5-1s improvement

improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Major tracking accuracy improvement, but significant architectural change

failed_approaches.description: Increased max_velocity from 10.0 to 12.0 AND initial time allocation from 0.6 to 0.7 simultaneously. Trajectory became too aggressive for kinematic sim PD controller — max tracking error jumped to 6.4m and gate pass rate dropped to 67%.
failed_approaches.lesson: Match trajectory aggressiveness to controller capability. Change one parameter at a time.

failed_approaches.description: Curvature-aware initial time allocation had no measurable impact because L-BFGS optimizer in _optimize_time_allocation re-optimizes times regardless of initial guess.
failed_approaches.lesson: Initial time allocation heuristic matters less than the optimizer that runs after it.

failed_approaches.description: transition_time = max(times[i], times[i+1]) for acceleration estimation at segment boundaries.
failed_approaches.lesson: The acceleration estimate at segment boundaries serves as a feasibility proxy. Modifying it causes divergence.
failed_approaches.reason: Optimizer produced trajectories too fast for kinematic sim to follow

failed_approaches.description: transition_time = avg(times[i], times[i+1]) for acceleration estimation.
failed_approaches.lesson: Both max and average transition_time variants cause the same problem.
Increasing time_weight alone is insufficient without relaxing acceleration penalty.
Wide offset ranges distort waypoint geometry.
Short segments near gate centers cause L-BFGS to over-slow.

failed_approaches.description: L-BFGS curvature-speed penalty using waypoint-level turn angles.
failed_approaches.lesson: Waypoint-level angles are diluted by entry/exit points.
failed_approaches.reason: Penalty too broad or too weak

failed_approaches.description: time_weight increased from 2.0 to 2.5 in L-BFGS.
failed_approaches.lesson: L-BFGS is sensitive to time_weight — higher weight redirects convergence.
failed_approaches.reason: L-BFGS converged to worse local minimum

failed_approaches.description: Drag compensation (Faessler 2018): drag_coefficient * vel added to accel_des.
failed_approaches.lesson: Cancelling drag on CURRENT velocity removes beneficial velocity damping.
failed_approaches.reason: Sim drag provides free velocity damping that helps controller

failed_approaches.lesson: Helix section needs substantial time inflation for PD controller.
failed_approaches.reason: Helix gates need more inflation than 10% allows

failed_approaches.description: Reference-velocity drag feedforward (vff * ref_vel added to accel_des). Tested vff=0.1, 0.15, 0.5. All regressed.
failed_approaches.lesson: Velocity feedforward is mathematically correct at steady state but helix is all transients.
failed_approaches.reason: Helix is transient-dominated; velocity FF increases overshoot at turns.

failed_approaches.description: Gain scheduling (curvature-based and error-based) in kinematic sim. 16+ configs across 2 gain-scheduling approaches. Also tested FF attenuation (4 configs), predictive position targeting (14 configs), integral term PID (5 configs), dual-timescale FF (committed then reverted).
failed_approaches.lesson: Gain scheduling fundamentally doesn't work in kinematic sim without attitude dynamics. The feedforward direction is already optimal; changing gains redirects clamped acceleration away from optimal. Dual-timescale FF worked on one trajectory but regressed on another — controller tuning must be robust to trajectory variation.
failed_approaches.reason: No attitude dynamics in kinematic sim. Trajectory optimizer non-determinism across sessions.

failed_approaches.description: Racing line offset=0.6 with smoothness_weight=0.3 (fast basin). Produces 12.78s trajectory but gate-7 error 0.971m — worse than baseline.
failed_approaches.lesson: The racing line L-BFGS has two distinct local minima: fast (12.78s, high tracking error) and smooth (17.4s, low tracking error). The fast basin produces a trajectory too aggressive for the kinematic sim PD controller.
failed_approaches.reason: Fast trajectory creates untrackable curvature in helix

failed_approaches.description: Uniform time compression (3-15% compression of all segments). Even 3% was infeasible because some turn segments are already at acceleration limits.
failed_approaches.lesson: Compression must be segment-selective — only speed up segments with velocity headroom. Turn segments are already at their dynamic limits.
failed_approaches.reason: Turn segments at acceleration limits prevent any uniform speedup

failed_approaches.description: Polynomial curvature (κ = |v × a| / |v|³) for TOPP speed profiling. Curvature was artificially low because polynomial coefficients are timing-dependent — slow trajectory 'straightens out'.
failed_approaches.lesson: Polynomial curvature is timing-dependent and does NOT reflect geometric path curvature. Use waypoint Menger curvature for timing-independent speed profiling.
failed_approaches.reason: Polynomial curvature at slow timing gives near-zero values, producing no compression

failed_approaches.description: Curvature-dependent compression floors (0.65 straights / 0.80 turns) for TOPP retimer.
failed_approaches.lesson: Curvature-dependent floors are too conservative — TOPP speed limits already handle curvature-aware slowdown. Uniform floor is better.
failed_approaches.reason: Produced only 14.30s vs 13.50s with uniform 0.65 floor

failed_approaches.description: a_centripetal reduction (10.0→9.0) in TOPP retimer to limit turn speeds after FOV relaxation removal.
failed_approaches.lesson: max_compression floor (0.65) is the binding constraint on helix speed, not the curvature-based speed limits. Reducing a_centripetal has zero effect when max_compression dominates.
failed_approaches.reason: max_compression floor is binding constraint, not curvature speed limits
